file AI-cyber action plans The dominant development of the last 24 hours is confirmation by South Korea's Financial Services Commission that 16 financial firms — banks, savings banks, a credit-finance company, P2P lenders, an e-payment provider and two virtual-asset businesses — were breached in a campaign that regulators publicly characterise as AI-assisted, with roughly 100,000 customer records exposed. This is the first time a national financial regulator has attributed an intrusion campaign of this shape to agentic AI tooling in an official setting, and it is the reference case the sector should be reading this week. Two other items in the window matter for control design rather than for their victim count. In India, CERT-In's advisory on the abuse of payout and fund-transfer APIs describes attackers calling disbursement endpoints from the victims' own whitelisted infrastructure, bypassing loan creation, KYC, sanctions, beneficiary and per-transaction limit checks entirely. That is a business-logic bypass rather than a software exploit, and it transfers to any institution exposing disbursement APIs. In Europe, a Unit 42 report describes an unnamed bank entered through weak authentication on an externally managed third-party gateway , followed by months of undetected reconnaissance. Both describe failures of authorisation and monitoring, not of patching. The regulatory backdrop is tightening on the same theme. The ECB's action plans on AI-enabled cyber threats are due by 31 October , and the ECB letter names frontier-model exploit generation as the driver. US and European supervisors are separately questioning banks about their own use of AI agents. For most institutions the binding near-term deadline is the ECB one; the strategic exposure is that AI-assisted intrusion is no longer a forecast in supervisory documents but an evidenced incident pattern. That reframing carries a concrete expectation: demonstrable recovery capability, not just prevention. The ECB's action-plan deadline of 31 October sits fifteen days out. The catalogue is still version 2026.10.30 with 1,766 entries . Critique: that does not mean risk fell. The UTA0576 chain has been exploited since 3 October. It is still the main edge-VPN risk in this window. A patch stops future use of the flaw. It does not show whether the system was already breached. 2 — Binance is in recovery. Chainalysis was breached in a separate incident. Binance resumed withdrawals in phases on 1 November, across 15 networks . It says it has replaced ~95% of the ~$6.3bn stolen, up from ~90%. A full proof-of-reserves report is expected on 3 November . Critique: the ~95% figure is Binance's own claim. It is not independently audited. A proof of reserves, when it comes, will show holdings on one date. It will not show all debts. Separately, Chainalysis said on 30 October, reported 1 November, that an attacker used “offensive agentic techniques” to reach customer names, emails, user IDs and role labels. That data could help target the investigators tracing the Binance funds. Chainalysis says investigation content, passwords, MFA secrets and session tokens were not accessed. It also says its incident is not related to Binance . Critique: those limits are also Chainalysis's own claims. They have not been independently checked in the sources read. 3 — New risks: a CVSS 10.0 cloud bypass, and an exploited payment flaw Canonical LXD / MicroCloud CVE-2026-112816 (CVSS 10.0) was reported on 1 November. An attacker with network access to the HTTPS API can pose as a trusted client without its private key. Fixed snaps are out. Critique: a score of 10.0 shows how bad the flaw could be. Chainalysis began phased restoration of KYT and address screening on 6 November, with password resets, API-key rotation and IP allowlisting required; Reactor and Data Solutions remain offline. Binance’s Recovery Update #9 reopened more withdrawals, and Binance announced on 6 November that the zero-knowledge proof for its 44-token proof-of-reserves snapshot has been generated — though the public proof-of-reserves page still showed blank verification fields late on 6 November, so live user verification was not yet confirmed. The MetaEncryptor ransomware group listed US insurer Pekin Insurance, and N0n published what it says are 217,000 documents from US insurance brokerage Higginbotham. Arkéa was reached directly through a service provider’s platform — Fortuneo and human error are ruled out — and the bank says it has recovered part of the funds, without saying how much. Kaiser Ng leaves after more than five years, replaced by Justin Yek; Binance presents the handover as planned before the hack, not caused by it. Elliptic says attackers have converted about $175 million of stolen altcoins into about 2,300 BTC, though Arkham’s labelled wallets show far less — the two trackers measure different things and the gap is unresolved. The 44-token proof-of-reserves snapshot is now confirmed live, with every token at or above 100% backing. Chainalysis has brought Reactor back online alongside KYT and address screening, and Nubank’s crypto service is restored while Mercado Pago’s is not confirmed. ARTEX is an open-source, LLM-driven agentic pentesting framework in use by malicious actors since at least August 2026. The FBI’s FLASH-20261113-001 names financial services among ten targeted sectors, cites a South Korean financial-sector campaign that exposed personal data of about 67,000 people, and the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise that reached 2,250+ downstream customer environments. Talos counts more than 2,500 ARTEX-associated C2 IP addresses and says campaigns range from opportunistic scanning to targeted intrusion and supply-chain activity, including Storm-3358 hitting financial organisations in Southeast Asia. Some intrusions went from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours. The framework needs almost no operator skill, which is the point: it compresses the time banks have to detect and respond, and it often leaves no known indicators behind. 2 The RMM crisis is now a second wave, and the N-able chains are being exploited faster than vendors can patch. Microsoft published its own teardown of SCKit, the worm abusing cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels, and Huntress reported a second wave on 13 Nov — 205 hosts across 41 organisations, a new installer host and new markers. The technician-trap spread remains designed behaviour, not an observed infection path. Separately, the N-able 4EverAble2Shell chain was exploited within about five hours of its public PoC: researchers count 21 production N-central servers mining Monero, 19 of them already on Hotfix 2, while N-able says it has seen no compromise using the new flaws and has still not shipped a fix. The one solid control is disabling the Legacy API, which is not the default. CISA added the Check Point Gaia privilege-escalation flaw chained with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-123039) to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue on 13 Nov. 3 A wave of confirmed financial-sector breaches landed overnight, led by India’s largest bank. State Bank of India filed a police case a month after hackers stole a 375,000-record set from its Global IT Centre; only 3,897 records in that set have been confirmed to hold customer personal data, and the bank says no account numbers, balances, passwords, one-time codes, card data, PAN or Aadhaar were in the identified records — the 375,000 figure is the size of the dark-web dataset, not a confirmed victim count. KB Capital in South Korea confirmed a breach of 1,811 people, and Brazil’s National Treasury confirmed a leak of about 30,000 registrations and about 4,000 Pix keys. INC Ransom claimed Raymond James, Game Changer Wealth and Jamaica’s JETS payment network — all unverified. Trezor confirmed hardware implants in three Safe 5 wallets sold by a Southeast Asian reseller. Singapore’s CSA says reported cyber incidents have tripled since September. Binance has still not published Recovery Update #10 or its full zero-knowledge proof, while the US Justice Department says more than $2.7bn of the stolen funds have been frozen. CISA urged immediate patching of CVE-2026-114938 (“Java4Shell”), a memory-corruption flaw in the HotSpot JVM’s Base64 decoder that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution; Oracle released fixed builds on 17 November as part of its November CPU, and no in-the-wild exploitation had been confirmed as of 17 November. Java underpins core banking, payments and identity systems, and bundled runtimes in containers and appliances may not appear in software inventories. Separately, CISA added Perforce Puppet Enterprise CVE-2026-115731 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 17 November — a deserialization flaw letting any client with a CA-signed agent certificate run code on the Puppet Server, with a working proof of concept published by the researchers and a federal due date of 1 December. Rakuten Securities said on 17 November that data held in a test environment may have leaked on 11 November: up to about 11.25 million accounts’ login IDs, and up to about 4.47 million accounts with names, withdrawal bank accounts, declared income and financial-asset data, including former customers. No passwords or PINs are confirmed leaked and no unauthorised transactions attributable to the incident have been confirmed; the cause is under investigation. In the Optimizely attack, disclosed in this window, a flaw in the Experimentation signup flow let an attacker inject a crypto wallet-address clipper, a card skimmer and a cookie stealer into snippets served from Optimizely’s own CDN to visitors of 178 organisations’ sites, including HSBC, Equifax and Ledger. Optimizely confirmed the incident on 17 November and says the flaw is fixed and the code removed; how many card details were actually taken is unknown. Irish credit unions were also hit through their supplier Wellington IT, whose CU Online platform was exploited to retrieve saved payee records. 3 Korea’s regulator escalated after the hacking wave, and two senior voices warned that AI agents moving money could outrun bank controls. South Korea’s Financial Supervisory Service called in CISOs and security officers from 227 electronic-finance and 47 online investment-linked firms on 17 November, disclosed new incidents at Spoon (Giftiell, about 18,000 people’s data) and Zoomfund (about KRW 300 million in customer deposits), and began surprise on-site inspections of high-risk branches at four banks — the first in about ten years. The Financial Services Commission will require large firms to run vulnerability assessments twice a year instead of once, and to identify and classify all IT assets. Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr warned that AI agents able to move money without human approval could accelerate deposit flight into bank runs unfolding in minutes, and former MAS chief Ravi Menon said banks must set strict limits on agent autonomy over clients’ money. Neither is an observed incident — both are warnings about a control gap that is already appearing in practice.
